items.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, posted on his personal website that the company's AI software, Claude, helped him prove the 19th-century Riemann hypothesis over roughly six weeks. He described Claude as outpacing him near the finish line and linked to computer code written in Lean that he said could verify the findings, prompting other mathematicians to begin attempting confirmation of the proof. The claim was made one day after Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq stock market index; Alpöge acknowledged that this timing was unfortunate and wished he had finished earlier. The Riemann hypothesis concerns prime numbers—whole numbers greater than 1 that can only be divided by themselves and 1—and how they are distributed along the number line, with a formula for estimating their count below a given value. It is one of seven Millennium Prize problems selected in 200 by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has offered $1 million for each solved problem. The claim remains unconfirmed as mathematicians work to verify it; Alpöge's proof relies on code that others are testing rather than an established result. Separately, Italian mathematician Alessandro Masullo released an incomplete Riemann hypothesis proof he had worked on nearly 12 years without using AI due to distrust of the system. Other mathematicians have expressed discomfort with relying on AI for such problems and with lucrative private companies funding them; OpenAI previously claimed a non-public version of its tools helped solve part of another Millennium Prize problem, spending $15 million to employ 10,000 AI systems. University of Warwick's James Robinson criticized these efforts as immature boasting underpinned by billions of dollars and potential environmental damage.
items.title: Anthropic Mathematician Claims Claude Helped Prove Riemann Hypothesis

items.summary: Tesla officially launched in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage, while Elon Musk joined by video from his plane and stalling after about two minutes without delivering a real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that had just gone on sale. The event took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires' La Boca neighborhood; Musk opened positively but then said he did not know what to say, briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil company YPF, and thanked the audience before the feed cut off without him saying goodbye. Milei attempted to recover by telling the crowd that 'those who do a lot, talk little' and calling Musk 'the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.' The clip spread quickly online, with one post racking up over 1.1 million views overnight. Tesla opened orders Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y imported from Gigafactory Shanghai priced at $40,990 (Model 3 RWD), $43,990 (Model Y Premium RWD), $46,490 (Model 3 Premium Long Range), $49,990 (Model Y Premium Long Range), and $53,990 (Model 3 Performance), with about $600 in fees added on top. First deliveries are not expected until March or April 2027; sales occur online through showrooms at the Unicenter and Alcorta Shopping malls, as there are no dealers. Argentina is Tesla's fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay (which launched in July), though BYD already leads the country's EV market following Milei's government cutting import taxes on electric vehicles. The article suggests Musk's discomfort reflects a broader shift toward robotaxis and Optimus robots rather than car sales, noting Tesla's deliveries fell 8.6% to 1.636 million in 2025 as its second annual decline.
items.title: Musk stalls awkwardly during Tesla's Argentina launch

items.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspended the food licences of two dark stores operated by Amazon and BigBasket on Sinhagad Road, Pune, after Saturday inspections under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Officials reported violations of Schedule IV hygiene and sanitation requirements, citing expired products, fungal growth, unhygienic storage conditions, and inadequate pest control at both facilities. The suspension was reportedly taken against dark stores located on Sinhagad Road under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Authorities said both establishments violated provisions of Schedule IV, which outlines hygiene and sanitation requirements for food businesses.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Amazon and BigBasket Dark Store Licences in Pune

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to hold discussions with non-banking finance company executives on Monday, November 23, as part of its periodic dialogue with the banking and financial services sector. Governor Sanjay Malhotra along with all deputy governors are anticipated to be present for the meeting, which will include senior NBFC executives, housing finance companies, and microfinance institutions. These interactions typically lack a specific agenda but provide an opportunity for industry officials and regulators to share developments, concerns, and emerging challenges. BFSI companies have reported strong earnings with robust balance sheets overall, though several areas of concern remain. A deficit monsoon this year has cast doubt on the rural economy, potentially impacting microfinance companies and rural-focused NBFCs; some MFIs are observing drought-affected areas in Maharashtra while watching how the north west monsoon will affect agriculture across other states. On regulatory matters, some microfinance institutions may seek to replace the Rs 3 lakh household income cap with state-linked thresholds, though households earning up to Rs 3 lakh currently qualify for loans and monthly loan repayment is capped at 50% of income. Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu noted that any revision would depend on RBI's assessment and industry developments, while cautioning that excluding certain loans from the repayment-to-income ratio could undermine its purpose of preventing over-indebtedness. Cybersecurity also features as a rising challenge across the financial industry, with at least two large banks reporting data leaks recently alongside past incidents among small NBFCs; as AI usage grows, RBI may want to understand lenders' efforts to strengthen systems against future attacks. Gold loan companies' continued strong growth could be discussed too, particularly given recent gold price crashes and some firms flagging early signs of stress.
items.title: RBI to Meet NBFCs on November 23: Microfinance Stress, Gold Loans and Cybersecurity Risks in Focus

items.summary: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra, speaking at a Bank of Maharashtra event in Pune on November 21, 2026, urged banks to focus more lending on small and micro businesses rather than large enterprises. He argued that directing Rs 1,000 crore to a single large business would benefit only one entity, whereas the same amount given to small enterprises could yield benefits at least a hundred times greater, or up to a thousand times if distributed among micro-enterprise borrowers. Framing this as a 'special appeal,' he emphasized that development must be inclusive and reach all sections of society and regions. Malhotra also highlighted financial inclusion gains from the government's initiative having opened over 60 crore accounts, noting that needs now extend beyond account ownership to include digital literacy and caution in using digital banking services. He warned against fraudulent schemes promising returns of 20 per cent, 30 per cent or even 40 per cent over short periods, advising people not to share OTPs or respond to suspicious links. The remarks were made at a financial inclusion camp held at Waksai village that drew over 500 attendees; Malhotra said such camps would continue across the country until December 31 as part of the DFS's Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign.
items.title: RBI Governor Malhotra Urges Banks to Prioritize Small-Business Lending for Broader Economic Impact

items.summary: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) ordered an immediate halt to excavation and construction at the Adani Group's 1,500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project in Satara district. In a notice dated November 20, the MPCB directed the company to stop all ongoing and proposed work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Savarghar village (Sawarghar), Patan taluka, after an inspection by its Satara officials found that activities—including arrangements for a temporary labour camp and storage facilities—were being carried out without mandatory consent or permissions. The notice states the board's Satara sub-regional officer proposed legal action against the company for excavating and developing land without approval, noting it had not obtained environmental clearance for those two survey plots. Work cannot resume without MPCB prior approval, with further violations inviting legal proceedings.
items.title: MPCB Halts Adani's Tarali Pumped Storage Project Work Over Environmental Violations
